messages:
lee: FYI customer reported odd billing: a long streaming session with a tool call ended up showing tokens split across two different toolcall ids, one of which was billed but never returned a tool result.
jordan: Hmm. Are we generating a new toolcall_id on reconnect? Our dedupe keys are (session_id, toolcall_id). If toolcall_id changes on reconnect we can split attribution.

anya: I traced one of the traces. Runtime emits TOOL_CALL_STARTED with toolcall_id=null on initial attempt (we attach temp id client-side), then on reconnect the router injected a new toolcall_id: tc-8a3. Downstream accepted and then we later saw TOOL_CALL_RESULT associated to the original client id. Ledger saw confirmed tokens for tc-8a3 and left provisional for the client id orphaned.

anya: Event sample: ```json
{"event":"TOOL_CALL_STARTED","session":"st-7c3d","toolcall_id":null,"offset":512}
{"event":"TOOL_CALL_STARTED","session":"st-9d0f","toolcall_id":"tc-8a3","offset":512}
{"event":"TOOL_CALL_RESULT","session":"st-7c3d","toolcall_id":"client-tc-1","tokens":42}
```

maria: Ugh. So two issues: router creating a new toolcall id that isn't reconciled with the original client id, and ledger not joining by parent_toolcall_id.
jordan: Proposed short-term: ledger treat toolcall events with matching offsets as the same logical toolcall when within a 30s window and session.parent_toolcall present. Longer term: propagate parent_toolcall_id header.

lee: Customers will see mismatched spend lines and 'missing tool result' in the console. UX ask: mark sessions with 'toolcall splintered' and show both toolcall ids in the debug export.

ops-bot: Ticket created: BILL-1250 "Split toolcall attribution on reconnects" assigned to anya. Priority P2.

anya: Implementation plan: 1) router: stop generating fresh toolcall_ids on reconnect unless the client explicitly requested new toolcall; 2) add X-Parent-Toolcall header when resuming; 3) billing: accept parent_toolcall join key for provisional dedupe for 45s. Add metric billing.toolcall.split_detected.

jordan: Test matrix: reconnect w/ same model, reconnect causing model-swap, reconnect during toolcall streaming, reconnect with client-supplied id. Also include truncated toolcall where runtime closes stream early (EOF) and then a retry feeds remainder.

maria: For console: add a column in debug CSV "toolcall_ids" that lists observed ids and a flag "splintered". We'll need to be careful with PII but ids are fine.

anya: Quick SQL to find suspects: 
```
select session, array_agg(distinct toolcall_id) as ids, sum(tokens) as total_tokens, count(*) as events
from toolcall_events
where event_time > now() - interval '14 days'
and toolcall_id is not null
group by session
having cardinality(array_agg(distinct toolcall_id)) > 1
order by total_tokens desc
limit 100;
```
Share to ops channel to triage.

lee: If we change router behaviour, watch for any cases where clients intentionally re-issue toolcalls and expect a new id. Need a feature flag billing.toolcall_reconnect_guard.
jordan: Agreed. Canary in eu-west-1, add alert if toolcall_success_rate drops by >1%.

maria: Action items: anya implement router change + parent header, jordan add ledger join-key and metric, lee add export column + ops runbook, I'll update release notes. We'll sync in tomorrow's infra standup.
billing-bot: Note: operations impact analysis added to BILL-1250.

lee: One more note: this intersects truncation: if a reconnect leads to a truncated resume (we drop a few tokens) our charge accounting must reconcile partial token ranges. Add tests covering truncation overlap detection.
maria: Good call. Add to test plan. Thanks everyone.
